name: Giza pyramid complex, Egypt
note: Approximate Old Kingdom pyramid-building era. Dates are broad teaching ranges, not a reconstruction of a specific year.

name: Imperial Rome, Italy
note: A simplified interval for the Roman imperial era in the West. This marker does not depict the city's changing footprint or imperial borders.

name: Classic-period Tikal, Guatemala
note: A broad Classic-period Maya context. Site histories and chronology are more complex than this teaching interval.

name: Stonehenge stone circle, England
note: Teaching window around the stone-circle construction near 2500 BCE. Earlier earthworks and later alterations are not represented by this interval.

name: Classical Acropolis, Athens, Greece
note: A broad fifth-century BCE context for major Classical monuments. This is a selected building era, not the complete history of the hill.

name: Borobudur, Indonesia
note: A rounded eighth- to ninth-century temple-building context. The modern view includes later conservation and does not show an ancient reconstruction.

name: Angkor, Cambodia
note: Broad context for Khmer capitals from the ninth through fifteenth centuries. A single marker cannot portray their changing extent or each monument’s construction date.

name: Lalibela churches, Ethiopia
note: A thirteenth-century context for the rock-cut churches. Lalibela remains a place of worship; the teaching interval does not mark the end of its history.

name: Great Zimbabwe, Zimbabwe
note: A rounded eleventh- to fifteenth-century context for this Shona urban and trading centre. Its full chronology is more complex than the selected teaching interval.

name: Rapa Nui monumental landscape, Chile
note: A broad monumental-building window following UNESCO’s tenth- to sixteenth-century overview. Chronologies vary; this is not a settlement-date claim or an ancient landscape reconstruction.
